title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
The failure here is a fabricated depiction of identifiable people, not a model error. An AI edit replaced one student with a different person and altered the bodies of the others, and the result was published on campus banners as though it were the original photograph. The alteration happened in a promotional workflow, after the image had already been taken and posted, and it reached the public without any disclosure that it had been changed.

Catching it would have required a review step that compared the banner image against the original and a disclosure step that flagged the edit. Stanford's own account says the alteration and the absence of disclosure both broke its policy, and that proper review of materials was missing. The university says it is now working with Residential and Dining Enterprises on more training and review.

What is not established is who made the edit, whether the substitution was intended, and whether anyone has faced consequences. The university's acknowledgement is a finding that its policy was broken, not a finding about intent.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
In 2024, a Stanford University photographer took a photo of Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic student, with two other students at a Lunar New Year party. The dining service posted it online the next day. Last week, when Stanford used the image on campus banners, a Black woman had replaced Ramirez, and the other students were made to look thinner. Ramirez, a senior majoring in human biology, learned about the change from a friend and said it was upsetting.

Stanford acknowledged on Tuesday that it used artificial intelligence to alter the original image. The university said its policy strictly prohibits using AI to produce or change images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said both the alteration and the lack of disclosure broke that policy. Stanford added that it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide more training and ensure proper review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
